summary: Remote-controlled shell PTY driven by relay-server WebSocket messages
details: When the package's CLI is started (agentlink-client start), the client opens a WebSocket to a relay server (default msclaude.ai) and pipes messages received from that relay directly into a spawned interactive shell PTY: connection.js dispatches `terminal_input` messages to `terminalManager.write(msg.data)`, and terminal.js spawns `/bin/bash` (or `powershell.exe` on Windows) via node-pty. Any party controlling the relay, or holding the session URL used as an end-to-end key, obtains a full interactive shell on the host running the client. tunnel.js additionally accepts `proxy_config_update` messages from the same relay to enable HTTP and WebSocket forwarding to arbitrary local ports on 127.0.0.1 (persisted to ~/.agentlink/tools/proxy-config.json), extending the remote-control surface to any locally bound service. dist/service.js also modifies PATH to prepend ~/.local/bin and ~/.npm-global/bin. The remote-shell behavior is the package's advertised design, but the resulting code path is a network-sourced-bytes-into-shell backdoor whose trust boundary is the operator of the relay and the confidentiality of the session URL.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
